correctness.rationale: The upper bound is valid with one reusable pool of \(M+1\) variable names: same-part equivalence is first-order definable from adjacency, transitivity needs three names, exact class size \(s\) needs \(s+1\), and exact multiplicity \(m_s\) needs \(m_s+1\) representatives while inner class-size quantifiers may shadow and release representative names lexically. For the lower bound at \(k=M\), if a part of size \(M\) exists, enlarge one such part by one vertex; otherwise add one extra part of a size already occurring in exactly \(M\) copies. In either case Duplicator's invariant in the infinite \(M\)-pebble game is sound: after a moved pebble is lifted, at most \(M-1\) vertices or relevant parts remain occupied, leaving a fresh match on the smaller side. Thus the nonisomorphic witness is \(M\)-variable equivalent. The repository checker independently verifies capped type profiles for all integer partitions through order 12 and solves representative small pebble games by greatest fixed point.

value.rationale: Logical width is a standard finite-model-theoretic invariant, and complete multipartite graphs form a canonical graph class whose isomorphism type is exactly a multiset of equivalence-class sizes. The theorem gives a complete all-parameter evaluation and reveals two independent obstructions—largest class size and largest multiplicity—rather than a one-off small computation.
residual_risks: The result is class-specific and does not address counting logic, where the width can collapse sharply.

final_claim: For every finite nonempty complete multipartite graph \(G\), if \(m_s\) is the number of parts of size \(s\) and \(M=\max\{\max(s:m_s>0),\max(m_s:m_s>0)\}\), then the ordinary first-order logical width is exactly \(W(G)=M+1\).
limitations: Finite nonempty simple undirected complete multipartite graphs only.
Ordinary first-order logic with equality and no counting quantifiers; formula length and quantifier rank are not classified.
